methodology: The synthesis of novel cis-rich poly(vinyl thioether ester)s (PVTEEs) was achieved through thiol-yne click polymerization of diphenthiols and dipropiolates under controlled conditions, including regulation of substrates, catalysts, and reaction solvents. The photoisomerization process involved alternating irradiation at specific wavelengths to induce cis-to-trans isomerization.
research_objective: To synthesize novel unsaturated polymers with reversible cis-trans isomerization capability for potential applications in information storage and encoding.

key_findings.finding: Thiol-yne click polymerization of diphenthiols and dipropiolates to synthesize cis-rich poly(vinyl thioether ester)s (PVTEEs)
Polymer backbone with vinyl thioether ester moieties undergo reversible photoisomerization under alternating irradiation at 420 nm and 365 nm wavelengths, affording cis-rich and trans-rich PVTEEs
Chemical depolymerization of resultant PVTEEs can be realized via transesterification, selectively affording vinyl thioether diesters with good isolated yields
Thio-yne click polymerization can be used for synthesizing novel poly(vinyl thioether ester)s with high stereoselectivity and conversion rates.
Cis-rich PVTEEs could be reversibly isomerized under ambient conditions, influenced by the cis-trans stereoconfiguration of unsaturated polymers.
The cis-3 isomer is more thermodynamically stable than the trans-3 isomer.
The photo-induced cis-to-trans isomerization can be achieved with good yields and high stereoselectivity.
The cis/trans ratios were determined using 1H NMR analysis.
Photoluminescence quenching effect between cis-3 and TXO, as well as trans-3 and TXO was observed.
